Representative_Docs: ['How do I (34M) move forward with my daughter (now 9F) after escaping an abusive relationship with my ex (35F) who put us through hell? This is a crazy story and might be a bit long-winded, so I apologize in advance. Im posting here for advice on healing and moving onIve been through the wringer, and I need perspectives from folks whove been in similar situations.Back in 2022, I (now 34M) started dating this woman (now 35F), and in the beginning, it all seemed great. She was loving, kind, supportive toward me changing jobs, affectionate, and I felt a connection with her that Id never experienced beforeincluding in my 10-year marriage to my ex-wife.It felt like she was this perfect person. That was until about 6 months in, when she started having these episodes of extreme rage and emotional outbursts that were all over the place. She would become physically violent toward me, even in front of my daughter (7F at the time). The first time was on a vacation in Colorado in the fall of 2022, and it escalated from there. I later found out she suffers from Borderline Personality Disorder, as well as other disorders that dont mesh well with accountability.On top of the physical abuse and mental breakdowns (plenty of stories I could branch off on, but I wont right now), I also found out she was actively cheating on me with three different ex-boyfriends at the time. Id find out, shed cry, apologize, promise it would never happen again, and Id give her another chance. That happened at least four different times between 2022-2024.Cut to fall 2023: She became pregnant. The timeline didnt necessarily add up, but I love being a dad (I already have two daughters), and I was desperate for another child, so I ignored the warning signs and got excited.Two months later, while off her medication, she had another episode and assaulted me again. She refused to get help or be honest with her therapist, so I asked her to leave my house. She threw a fit but called her mom and got picked up.I figured shed calm down and apologize in a couple days, or at least wed co-parent once the baby arrived. Boy, was I wrong. A week or so later, I was served with a PPO (Personal Protection Order) accusing me of assaulting her. Completely caught off guardId never laid a hand on her like thatI decided to fight it.Three months later, the court sided with her because she made it seem like shed had an abortion, and they were concerned Id retaliate. At that point, I thought my child was dead, and I mourned them like they were. It was an incredibly painful time.Two weeks after that, I got an email from her begging for forgiveness, asking to come back, and saying we could be a family with the babywho was still alive. Stupidly, and desperate to be a dad again, I let her return. A week later, our baby boy was born.I cant properly express the joy I felt holding him for the first time. It was like he was brought back to life, and I finally felt like I could protect him.Over the next eight months, I loved him, provided for him, and was excited to raise himall while she still wasnt taking her medication seriously and continued having violent episodes (many recorded on my phone).Cut to fall 2024: One night, I brought up my concerns about her not taking her mental health, our relationship, or the kids well-being seriously. She lost it and spiraled. She shoved me multiple times against the kitchen counter, pulled out a knife, and made threats about harming herself (mainly suicide threats). This wasnt the first time shed threatened or attempted that, so I froze in fear. Then she went further, threatening to walk into traffic with the baby and see how you feel about that. This was the third time shed threatened to kill the baby.I lunged to get the knife away (successfully), grabbed her by one arm and her back, and walked her to the front door, screaming that shed gone too far, ruined everything, and I couldnt help her anymore. At the door, I told her to get out and that I never wanted to see her again. She froze, so I grabbed her shoes, put them in front of her, and repeated it.She bent down, put on her shoes, stood up, spit in my face, and swung at me wildly, causing me to fall against the wall. I regained my footing, held her down over the couch arm to stop the hits, opened the door with one hand, and backed up. She was in shock that I was serious. I stood her up and made her leave, but as she did, she confirmed what Id suspected but didnt want to believe: The baby wasnt mineit was her brother-in-laws (shed been living with him and her sister when she got pregnant). My heart sank, but I shut the door.Unsure what to do, I called the 988 suicide hotline to get her help, fearing shed try something. After about 10 minutes on the call, police knocked and said shed accused me of assault again. They arrested me.For the next 6 months, I collected every video, picture, voice memo, and handwritten apology note as evidence for a trial. I was ready to win and make it easier to get the boy back while holding her accountable. But a week before telling the court I wanted a trial, I found an envelope on my car with a picture of my daughters school inside. Knowing how unhinged she is, I took it as a threat to my daughters safety if I didnt take the plea deal.Not wanting to risk my daughters safety, I accepted the plea: 1 year probation, and at the end, my record is wiped clean like it never happened (because it didnt).Even though Im thankful to be out of that abusive relationship, the hardest part is not having the baby. Im 99% sure hes not biologically mine, but I had him for 8 months and loved him like he was. Plus, my daughter feels like her brother was stolen from her.Its been almost a year since the court stuff finalized, and my daughter and I are in a much better place physically and mentally. But I still feel sick every day knowing I dont have the baby and that this crazy person is walking free without consequences for all the evil things shes doneand could do to someone else. Its awful.Side note: Shes currently trying to be an online Christian influencer, reading the Bible for hours in a fake British accent. Doesnt seem like she ever got on those meds.TL;DR: Escaped a physically/emotionally abusive relationship with my ex who has BPD and cheated multiple times. She faked an abortion, lied about paternity, threatened suicide and harm to our (non-bio) baby, got me arrested falsely twice, and possibly threatened my daughter. Now free, but struggling with loss and injustice. How do my daughter and I properly move forward after this trauma?Any advice on therapy, co-parenting grief (even if not bio), protecting ourselves legally/emotionally, or just general healing tips? Representative_Docs: ['Good Men Dont And I Will No Longer Accept This After nine years of volatility, cruelty, and emotional, psychological, and verbal abuse, I am finally no contact.Weve been split for six months. Its only been a few weeks since I got the rest of my belongings back and cut contact for good. I tried to stay friends. I tried to be mature. I tried to believe that if I explained myself better, regulated better, healed harder, things would make sense.They didnt.The cognitive dissonance is real. You can miss the bond and still know it was unsafe. You can grieve and still choose no contact.So this is my line in the sand.Good men dont:Treat their partners pain about friends or family as an inconvenience.Yell during conflict as a way to dominate or control.Slam fists into hands, hit walls, destroy objects, or use intimidation to create fear.Use jealousy over psychiatric hospitalization (you got help and I didnt) as a weapon.Mock or invalidate therapy and healing progress.Undermine their partners body or self-worth during weight loss or physical change (he told me he wasnt attracted to skinny girls when I was losing weight).Compete with, resent, or feel threatened by their partners recovery.Allow others to manipulate or exploit their partner.Belittle, demean, or talk down to their partner.Threaten to call the police as punishment or leverage.Abandon their partner or create housing instability.Refuse to share financial and household responsibility while benefiting from their partners labor.Use weaponized incompetence so their partner carries everything.Escalate while their partner is begging for help.Hold someone hostage in arguments until theyre dizzy, confused, and blaming themselves.Pretend to seek help or change to prevent their partner from leaving.Switch personalities once cohabitation creates dependency.Self-harm or threaten self-harm to shift blame.Pressure someone to confess to things they did not do during a mental health crisis.Yell at their partner on the day they are released from psychiatric hospitalization.Initiate or engage in sex when their partner does not have the capacity to give informed consent.And good men do not weaponize mental health or law enforcement to regain control when their partner finally stops accepting mistreatment.When I refused to accept an apology after being yelled at, police were called on me under the claim that I was in psychosis.
